      <content name="FullSummary"><p>You have two <span class="qt0">kidneys</span>. They are fist-sized organs on either side of your backbone above your waist. The tubes inside filter and clean your blood, taking out waste products and making urine.  <span class="qt0">Kidney</span> <span class="qt1">cancer</span> forms in the lining of tiny tubes inside your <span class="qt0">kidneys</span>. </p><p><span class="qt0">Kidney</span> <span class="qt1">cancer</span> becomes more likely as you age. Risk factors include smoking, having certain genetic conditions, and misusing pain medicines for a long time.</p><p>You may have no symptoms at first. They may appear as the <span class="qt1">cancer</span> grows. See your health care provider if you notice:</p><ul><li>Blood in your urine</li><li>A lump in your abdomen</li><li>Weight loss for no reason</li><li>Pain in your side that does not go away</li><li>Loss of appetite</li></ul><p>Tests to diagnose <span class="qt0">kidney</span> <span class="qt1">cancer</span> include blood, urine, and imaging tests. You may also have a biopsy.</p><p>Treatment depends on your age, your overall health and how advanced the <span class="qt1">cancer</span> is. It might include surgery, chemotherapy, or radiation, biologic, or targeted therapies.  Biologic therapy boosts your body's own ability to fight <span class="qt1">cancer</span>. Targeted therapy uses drugs or other substances that attack specific <span class="qt1">cancer</span> cells with less harm to normal cells.</p><p>NIH: National <span class="qt1">Cancer</span> Institute</p></content>
